sections.h2: Where is Cape Girardeau, and what is the housing market like?
sections.html:
Cape Girardeau sits on the west bank of the Mississippi River in Southeast Missouri, between St. Louis and Memphis along Interstate 55. The Census Bureau estimates 40,977 residents as of July 1, 2025, spread over about 29 square miles of land.

The housing numbers here run well below the other big Missouri cities. Homes are valued lower, more households rent, and a university and two large hospitals shape who is buying and moving.

With barely more than half of homes owner-occupied, a Cape Girardeau house that has been a rental is not unusual.

sections.h2: How did the river and the railroad shape Cape Girardeau?
sections.html:
A French trader named Jean Pierre Girardeau set up a post on a rocky bluff in the early 1760s, and the city takes its name from that cape. Louis Lorimier founded the community on January 4, 1793, under a Spanish land grant. The town was platted in 1806, incorporated in 1808 and made a city by the legislature in 1843.

Steamboats made it the largest port on the Mississippi between St. Louis and Memphis. The first railroad arrived in the early 1880s, and the city's population more than doubled between 1900 and 1920. The International Shoe Company factory built in 1907 gave the Red Star neighborhood its name, because many workers lived nearby.

Floods from the Mississippi hit the riverfront repeatedly between 1927 and 1951. The Army Corps of Engineers finished a floodwall and levee of more than a mile in 1964, and the city now owns and maintains it. The city's online maps include a flood zone layer, which is the place to check a parcel near the river.

sections.h2: Which employers and schools drive demand for Cape Girardeau houses?
sections.html:
Health care leads. St. Francis Medical Center employs about 3,143 people and Mercy Hospital Southeast about 2,950. Procter & Gamble, Southeast Missouri State University, Cape Girardeau Public Schools, Drury Hotels and Century Casino complete the list of large local employers.

The city is mostly in the Cape Girardeau Public Schools district, with a section of Cape Girardeau County in the Jackson R-II district. A small part of the city lies in Scott County, where Scott City R-I covers most of that area. Check your parcel before you tell a buyer which district applies.

  • Southeast Missouri State University has a main campus and a River Campus in the city.
  • The Cape Girardeau Regional Airport opened a new passenger terminal in 2024.
  • Local roads include Interstate 55, Kingshighway and the Bill Emerson Memorial Bridge, which opened in 2003.

sections.h2: What does the Cape Girardeau climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
The city has a humid subtropical climate. Average yearly precipitation is about 47.9 inches, spring is the wettest season, and the record high is 107 degrees on June 29, 2012. The airport sees about 47 days a year at 90 degrees or hotter.

That means air conditioning, attic ventilation, roof condition and basement dampness draw the most attention in a buyer inspection. Winters bring a mix of rain, sleet and snow, with about 12.8 days a year that never rise above freezing.

sections.h2: What rules does Cape Girardeau have for rental houses and repairs?
sections.html:
The city licenses residential rentals and enforces a checklist of safety and condition standards through Inspection Services at City Hall, 44 N. Lorimier Street, phone 573-339-6327. Standards include working smoke alarms in every bedroom, in the hallway outside bedrooms and on each floor, bedroom egress windows with a clear opening of at least 24 inches high and 30 inches wide, handrails on steps with four or more risers, and guards on landings more than 30 inches high.

If you are selling a house that has tenants, ask the department whether the license is current, because a buyer investor will want that answer.

For repair work, inspection requests received after 11:30 a.m. are scheduled for the next day, final inspections need 24 hours notice, and approved plans must be on site. The city became a Certified Local Government in 1991 and its Historic Preservation Commission reviews Certificate of Appropriateness applications in local historic districts. Ask the planning division whether your street is in one before you plan exterior changes.

sections.h2: How do Cape Girardeau County assessments and taxes work?
sections.html:
The county assessor, whose office is at 1 Barton Square, Suite 201 in Jackson, values every parcel. State law requires reassessment of existing real property as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year, and new improvements are added when construction finishes.

Tax rates come from the school, library, fire and other districts, not from the assessor. The assessor's website has a real estate search and parcel map, and the office handles the Missouri Property Tax Credit form 948 for qualifying seniors and disabled owners. Call 573-243-2468 or email appraisal@capecounty.us for value questions.

Ask the Cape Girardeau County Collector for your current bill, and ask the title company how the year will be split at closing.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded in Cape Girardeau County?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the county Recorder of Deeds at #1 Barton Square, Suite 203, Jackson, phone 573-243-8123, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Documents can be mailed, dropped off or e-recorded.

The recording fee for a standard document is $24 for the first page and $3 for each added page, and a document that misses the formatting standards carries an extra $25. Pages must be 8.5 by 11 inches, with a three inch margin on the first page left blank for the recorder's stamp. The office cannot create documents or give legal advice, so a title company or attorney drafts the deed.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a Cape Girardeau house fast?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself or take a direct cash offer. In a market with many renters and a lower price range, houses that need work or carry tenants can sit on the market, so some owners prefer a quick as-is sale.

Whichever route you choose, gather the rental license status, the county tax bill, the mortgage payoff and the school district for the address first. Those items settle most of the questions that come up between a signed contract and closing day.

faqs.q: Is Cape Girardeau in one county?
faqs.a: Mostly it is in Cape Girardeau County, but a small part of the city lies in Scott County. Check the parcel's county before calling an assessor or recorder.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Cape Girardeau house?
faqs.a: The Cape Girardeau County Recorder of Deeds in Jackson, at #1 Barton Square, Suite 203. A standard deed costs $24 for the first page and $3 for each extra page, plus $25 if formatting rules are not met.

faqs.q: How often does the county reassess my house?
faqs.a: State law requires reassessment as of January 1 of every odd-numbered year. The assessor also adds new improvements as construction finishes, so a remodel can change the value in any year.

faqs.q: Does my rental house need a license before I sell it?
faqs.a: The city requires residential rental licensing and inspects against a safety checklist. Call Inspection Services at 573-339-6327 to confirm your unit's status, since buyers who plan to keep tenants will ask.

faqs.q: What flood concerns affect Cape Girardeau homes?
faqs.a: Houses near the Mississippi River depend on the floodwall and levee built in 1964. The city publishes interactive maps with flood zone layers, so check your parcel there.
